label: adaptive
note: Illustrative stated starting points; live provider calls, no user Chart writes.

context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

raw.destination: Maintain a consistent workout routine with three 30-minute bodyweight sessions each week

waypoints.title: Exercise three times a week for 30 minutes each session
waypoints.rationale: Regular sessions establish the habit of consistent exercise
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete at least three 30-minute bodyweight exercise sessions each week for four consecutive weeks.
requirements: Complete three 30-minute bodyweight sessions each week
Maintain this routine for four consecutive weeks

moves.title: Schedule three 30-minute workout slots in your calendar this week
moves.rationale: Scheduling creates commitment and structure for workouts

moves.title: Prepare a simple bodyweight workout plan you can do at home
moves.rationale: Having a plan reduces decision fatigue and increases workout consistency

moves.title: Complete your first 30-minute workout session this week
moves.rationale: Starting the routine builds momentum

moves.title: Track each workout session to monitor consistency
moves.rationale: Tracking progress helps maintain motivation and accountability

suggestedOneMove.title: Schedule three 30-minute workout slots in your calendar this week
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Setting specific times makes it easier to commit and follow through

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus on establishing the habit by scheduling and completing three 30-minute bodyweight workouts weekly at home.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Exercises sporadically with availability for three 30-minute home bodyweight sessions weekly.
assumptions: User has basic knowledge of bodyweight exercises or can find simple routines online
User can allocate three 30-minute time slots weekly without financial cost
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: User completes three 30-minute workout sessions in one week.
analysis.difficultyReduction: Breaking the goal into scheduling, planning, starting, and tracking reduces overwhelm and supports habit formation.

results.error: All providers failed validation or generation

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

raw.destination: Successfully complete your first half marathon (21.1 km).

waypoints.title: Increase weekly running distance to 15 km
waypoints.rationale: Building endurance by increasing total weekly distance prepares your body for longer runs.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Run a total of 15 km across three running sessions in one week.

moves.title: Add a 3 km run on your third training day
moves.rationale: Start by adding a manageable additional run to increase weekly distance.

moves.title: Gradually increase one run to 6 km over two weeks
moves.rationale: Build endurance by extending one run beyond your current 5 km comfortably.

moves.title: Distribute remaining kilometers across the other two runs
moves.rationale: Balance your weekly distance to reach 15 km total without overexertion.

waypoints.title: Complete a 10 km run without stopping
waypoints.rationale: Running 10 km continuously demonstrates improved stamina necessary for longer distances.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Successfully run 10 km in one session without stopping.

moves.title: Choose a 10 km route and plan pacing
moves.rationale: Preparing the route and pace helps manage endurance during the run.

moves.title: Incorporate interval training to build stamina
moves.rationale: Intervals improve cardiovascular fitness and running efficiency.

moves.title: Run the 10 km route at a comfortable pace
moves.rationale: Executing the run tests your endurance progress.

waypoints.title: Complete a 15 km run comfortably
waypoints.rationale: A 15 km run shows readiness for the half marathon distance.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Successfully run 15 km in one session without excessive fatigue.

moves.title: Increase long run distance by 1-2 km each week
moves.rationale: Gradual distance increases prevent injury and build endurance.

moves.title: Maintain consistent pacing during long runs
moves.rationale: Consistent pace helps manage energy over longer distances.

moves.title: Incorporate rest days to aid recovery
moves.rationale: Recovery is essential to adapt to increased training load.

waypoints.title: Complete the half marathon distance (21.1 km)
waypoints.rationale: Successfully running the full half marathon distance achieves your goal.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Finish a 21.1 km run, completing the half marathon distance.

moves.title: Follow a tapering plan before race day
moves.rationale: Reducing training load before the event optimizes performance.

moves.title: Plan race day logistics and nutrition
moves.rationale: Preparation ensures focus and energy during the run.

moves.title: Run the half marathon at a sustainable pace
moves.rationale: Pacing strategy helps complete the race successfully.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add a 3 km run on your third training day
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Start by adding a manageable additional run to increase weekly distance.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Build your endurance gradually by increasing weekly distance and long run length before attempting the half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Comfortably running 5 km twice a week, training capacity of three days weekly, no prior half marathon completion.
assumptions: User can train three days per week consistently.
User has basic running experience but no half marathon experience.
User can gradually increase running distance safely.
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Current weekly running distance is 10 km (5 km twice).
analysis.difficultyReduction: Starting with a small increase in weekly running distance (adding a 3 km run) makes the first milestone achievable without overexertion.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

waypoints.title: Reach 200 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Establish initial growth beyond early adopters to validate product appeal and acquisition methods.

moves.title: Reach out to current users for feedback and referrals
moves.rationale: Engage existing users to improve product and encourage word-of-mouth growth.

moves.title: Implement basic referral incentives
moves.rationale: Encourage current users to invite others to Anchor.

moves.title: Optimize onboarding flow to reduce friction
moves.rationale: Improve user experience to increase conversion from signups to paying users.

moves.title: Analyze subscription analytics to identify drop-off points
moves.rationale: Use data to inform targeted improvements.

waypoints.title: Achieve consistent monthly retention rate above 70%
waypoints.rationale: Retention is critical for sustainable growth and recurring revenue.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Monthly retention rate remains above 70% for at least three consecutive months.

moves.title: Survey users who churn to identify pain points
moves.rationale: Understand reasons for user loss to address them effectively.

moves.title: Develop and release retention-focused features or content
moves.rationale: Add value that encourages continued subscription.

moves.title: Engage users regularly via email or in-app messages
moves.rationale: Maintain connection and remind users of Anchor's benefits.

moves.title: Monitor retention metrics monthly and adjust strategies
moves.rationale: Iterate based on data to improve retention.

waypoints.title: Establish a repeatable user acquisition channel yielding 100 new paying users monthly
waypoints.rationale: A reliable acquisition channel is necessary to scale user base sustainably without paid ads.
waypoints.completionCriteria: A user acquisition channel is documented and consistently delivers 100 new paying users per month.

moves.title: Experiment with content marketing (blog posts, social media)
moves.rationale: Attract organic traffic and leads.

moves.title: Leverage user testimonials and case studies
moves.rationale: Build trust and credibility to convert prospects.

moves.title: Optimize website SEO for relevant keywords
moves.rationale: Increase organic search visibility.

moves.title: Track and analyze acquisition sources
moves.rationale: Identify most effective channels to focus efforts.

waypoints.title: Grow paying users to 1,000 with sustainable retention and acquisition
waypoints.rationale: Scaling to 1,000 paying users confirms product-market fit and operational capacity for growth.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Paying users count reaches 1,000 with retention and acquisition metrics stable or improving.

moves.title: Refine product features based on user feedback
moves.rationale: Enhance value proposition to attract and retain more users.

moves.title: Increase outreach through partnerships or collaborations
moves.rationale: Expand reach without paid advertising.

moves.title: Improve onboarding and support processes
moves.rationale: Boost user satisfaction and conversion rates.

moves.title: Regularly review analytics to guide growth decisions
moves.rationale: Ensure data-driven strategy adjustments.

waypoints.title: Scale paying users to 10,000 with stable retention and repeatable acquisition
waypoints.rationale: Achieving 10,000 paying users realizes the vision of a sustainable Anchor business.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Paying users count reaches 10,000 with retention above 70% and repeatable acquisition channel active.

moves.title: Automate user engagement and support workflows
moves.rationale: Maintain quality service at scale.

moves.title: Expand content and community initiatives
moves.rationale: Foster user loyalty and organic growth.

moves.title: Continuously optimize acquisition channels based on performance
moves.rationale: Maximize efficiency and growth rate.

moves.title: Monitor financial metrics to ensure sustainability
moves.rationale: Balance growth with operational viability.

suggestedOneMove.title: Reach out to current users for feedback and referrals
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Engage existing users to improve product and encourage word-of-mouth growth.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus first on growing your paying user base to 200 by leveraging existing users and improving onboarding without paid ads.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users, solo developer, 10 hours/week, no paid ads, subscription analytics available.
assumptions: User feedback and referrals can drive initial growth.
Retention above 70% is achievable with targeted improvements.
Organic acquisition channels can be developed without paid ads.
Scaling requires operational improvements and automation.
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Current paying users are 20; growing to 200 is a feasible next step to validate growth methods.
analysis.difficultyReduction: Breaking growth into stages from 20 to 200, then 1,000, then 10,000 reduces complexity and risk.
